Note::TexAccessor::cmd_sub¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::TexAccessor::cmd_sub(std::string_view cmd,
                             std::string_view repl) const

Substitute One Control Word¶

cmd_sub(cmd, repl) replaces each lexical occurrence of one TeX control word with caller-provided text. It is the precise choice when the command name is known and its replacement is independent of attached arguments. It does not parse or consume {...} or [...] groups after the command, and it does not expand macro definitions. Use macro_subs() when declarations inside each cell should determine expansion; use strip_cmds() when command calls and their attached groups should disappear.

cmd accepts either alpha or \alpha. A terminal * is significant: alpha and alpha* select different tokens. The selector otherwise contains only ASCII letters or @; an empty selector, whitespace, punctuation, or an embedded backslash rejects before the receiver is read. Matching is exact and case-sensitive, so \alpha does not match \alphabet, \Alpha, or \alpha*. A doubled backslash protects the following text from being read as a control word.

repl is copied literally. Dollar signs, backslashes, braces, and $& have no regex replacement meaning. An empty replacement therefore removes only the selected control word while retaining any following groups. The operation is out-of-place, preserves dtype and shape, and leaves the receiver unchanged. It is not inherently idempotent: a replacement that contains the selected command can be matched by a later call.

Undefined state propagates after selector validation; defined non-Text input rejects. The kernel scans each cell once and allocates one output string per cell. Runtime is linear in source bytes plus bytes copied from repl.

Example 1: Exact Matching And Literal Replacement¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note({
    R"(\alpha + \alpha* + \alphabet + \\alpha)",
    R"(\alpha* + \alpha)",
    "plain"});
std::cout << source.tex().cmd_sub("alpha", "[$&]") << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["[$&] + \\alpha* + \\alphabet + \\\\alpha", "\\alpha* + [$&]", "plain"]

$& is copied as two ordinary characters. The starred token, longer command, and escaped spelling remain untouched.

Example 2: Starred Selection And Leading Backslash¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note({
    R"(\alpha + \alpha* + \alphabet + \\alpha)",
    R"(\alpha* + \alpha)",
    "plain"});
std::cout << source.tex().cmd_sub("alpha*", "STAR") << '\n';
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "leading slash same="
          << ((source.tex().cmd_sub("alpha", "A") ==
               source.tex().cmd_sub(R"(\alpha)", "A")).all().bool_item())
          << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["\\alpha + STAR + \\alphabet + \\\\alpha", "STAR + \\alpha", "plain"]
leading slash same=true

Example 3: Matrix Shape Is Preserved¶

const auto grid = pluss::make_note(
    std::vector<std::string>{R"(\alpha)", R"(\beta)", "",
                             R"(\alpha+\alpha)"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
std::cout << grid.tex().cmd_sub("alpha", "A") << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["A", "\\beta"],
  ["", "A+A"]
]

Example 4: Validation, Undefined State, And Dtype¶

try {
  (void)pluss::Note::undefined().tex().cmd_sub("bad name", "x");
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "cmd_sub(bad name): rejected\n";
}
std::cout << std::boolalpha << "undefined="
          << pluss::Note::undefined().tex().cmd_sub("alpha", "A").defined()
          << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1})
      .tex().cmd_sub("alpha", "A");
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "cmd sub Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

cmd_sub(bad name): rejected
undefined=false
cmd sub Int64: rejected
